topic: AI agents in advertising and CX
angle: Treat ‘sponsored agents’ as a service channel with incentives and guardrails—or you’ll buy engagement and lose trust.
linkedinPost:
“Sponsored agents” blur ads and service—and that’s the point.

OpenAI’s update shows marketers testing AI agents that guide discovery and purchases. For enterprises, this isn’t just a new ad unit; it’s a new service channel customers will judge like support.

My take from deployments: design for incentive alignment, not clicks. If the agent is paid to push inventory, it will. If it’s rewarded for customer fit and lifetime value, it behaves like your best associate.

Three must-haves: clear guardrails (what the agent won’t say/do), transparent sponsorship (no hidden steering), and measurement beyond CPA—think assisted revenue, NPS post-interaction, and return rate deltas.

Pilot with narrow intents (e.g., “find the right plan under $50”), human takeover at friction points, and a feedback loop that retrains off bad outcomes, not just engagement.

If you wouldn’t train a new rep that way, don’t launch an agent that way. Treat it as a service P&L with a brand risk budget.

How would you measure an ad-agent’s success beyond clicks? #CustomerExperience #AIStrategy #EnterpriseAI
xPost: Sponsored agents aren’t just ads—they’re a service channel. Align incentives to customer fit/LTV, add guardrails, and measure NPS + returns, not just CPA. If you wouldn’t train a rep that way, don’t launch the agent. #CustomerExperience #AIStrategy
